speech.text: Hurricane Elena makes landfall on Mexico's Yucatán coast.
Panama Canal reopens after a day-long closure.
Wildfire near Marseille forces thousands to evacuate.
Good afternoon, and welcome to World now.
I'm Paco Pixel, with Lola Byte.
Hurricane Elena has made landfall near Cancún with winds of one hundred and eighty kilometres per hour, according to Pixelburg Post.
Mexico's civil protection agency says about one point two million homes are without power and forty thousand people have gone to shelters.
Vic Vector, at our Americas desk, has the detail.
This is a life-threatening situation, the agency said.
The storm weakened slightly as it moved inland over the Yucatán peninsula.
Airports in Cancún and Mérida have closed, and hotels have moved guests to inner rooms.
Forecasters expect heavy rain over the next two days, with a risk of flooding in low areas.
The Panama Canal has reopened to ships after fog closed it for a day, Ledger Line reports.
The canal authority says about thirty ships are waiting to cross.
Shipping companies say the delays should clear within days.
Thick fog had forced the canal authority to stop all crossings, a rare step for the waterway.
Ships began moving again at dawn, with pilots guiding the first vessels through the locks at reduced speed.
